values: Radial orthogonality does not imply dual 1-conformal flatness — Alec Kriebel, v1.0.1. Preprint date and Zenodo publication: 2026-09-26. Explicit negative answer to Kurose’s printed Question 3(e): S²(1) × R with its Levi–Civita connection has integrable radial distributions but its dual is nowhere locally 1-conformally flat. Includes a non-self-dual example and n≥3 extension. Four-page unrefereed, AI-assisted preprint; two fresh adversarial AI reviews found no actionable issues. Exact and 403-check symbolic verifiers included. Historical priority unresolved; no first-resolution claim. Paper and materials: https://aleckriebel.github.io/Math/papers/radial-statistical-counterexample/
Byszewski, OWR54/2008 p3039; thesis2009 Q6.4.4; arXiv:1112.0352v1 Q4.4; catalogue30001113/OWR-2492-004: https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46200

A characteristic-two counterexample to dévissage for local deformation functors. Complete negative answer to the unrestricted fibre-product question using the additive F4 action and F2 subgroup; excludes every prorepresentable recipient. Prorepresentable-component variant unaddressed; nilpotent constant coordinate changes permitted. Known action, involution conjugacy and recipient collapse (Byszewski-Cornelissen2009 Props4.1/6.1) credited. Bounded priority, no exhaustive novelty guarantee. Extensive AI use; unrefereed; AI adversarial reviews, no conventional human peer review. Proof and verification: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/1024

30004549 / OWR-2654829-012. Three anti-invariant classes on a nonintegrable four-manifold. Compact smooth genus-two curve times elliptic curve; a smooth family tending to the product complex structure has nonintegrable members with h_J^- >= 3 for sufficiently small nonzero parameters. Negative answer to the unrestricted integrability clause; generic vanishing is the prior theorem of Tan, Wang, Zhang and Zhu. No exact h_J^-, fixed symplectic compatibility, analyticity, novelty, firstness or current-open certificate. Report33/2020 was actually released14September2021; bounded primary priority audit retains all access gaps. Extensive AI assistance; unrefereed; no independent human peer review or formal proof certification. All24 original files preserved. PR-declared4/5 is retained separately; native history and total historical count UNKNOWN; zero new author proof responses. https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/948 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422055

30002367 / OWR-12495-007: Totaro finite-group mod-p Chow detection degree equals greatest nonzero unstable-module suspension degree. Original OWR 32/2013 pp.1898–1899; precise Conjecture 12.8: https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46461?nt=1

Lannes’s T-functor and equivariant Chow rings — David Hemminger; Algebraic & Geometric Topology 21(4) (2021),1881–1910, published 18 August 2021. Prior affirmative answer: Proposition 6.1 with Theorem 5.6 and coarse Theorem 6.2(a), for every finite constant group, prime p and field k with char(k)≠p containing pth roots of unity. Grading is Chow codimension; suspension d is topological shift 2d. Exact field assumptions independently matched to Totaro 2014 Conjecture 12.8. Inspected arXiv:1911.03033v2; local centralizer/descent and operation qualifications retained in PR #1068. Journal body uninspected; no characteristic-p, missing-roots or integral extension certified. Existing publication; audit: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/1068

30002482 / OWR-12863-001: adjacent essentially Speh-paired ladder Langlands quotients have a symplectic period, in the historical characteristic-zero p-adic setting. Original Mitra OWR 03/2014 p.162: https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46494

Klyachko Models for Ladder Representations — Arnab Mitra, Omer Offen and Eitan Sayag; Documenta Mathematica 22 (2017),611–657. Published Theorem 10.3 (announced as 1.2) gives the full historical ladder assertion and its converse within the ladder class, in all ranks/cuspidal degrees, without unitarity or proper-ladder restrictions. Q=L after reversing increasing ladder order; adjacent Speh pairing becomes Δ2i−1=νΔ2i. Accepted historical field scope is characteristic 0, including residue characteristic 2; independently checked Mitra 2014 companion pp.435,437. OWR wording is unqualified; the journal states char(F)≠2, but positive/equal-characteristic extensions and separate general product necessity are not certified by this audit. Journal theorem inspected. Existing publication; audit: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/1146

30001214 / OWR-3397-002 and adjacent 30001215 / OWR-3397-003: Are maximal-spectrum symplectic cores locally closed, and does unrestricted Poisson Dixmier–Moeglin equivalence hold? Brown OWR 14/2009 pp.783–784: https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46215

Poisson algebras via model theory and differential-algebraic geometry — Jason Bell, Stéphane Launois, Omar León Sánchez and Rahim Moosa; Journal of the European Mathematical Society 19(7) (2017),2019–2049. Prior negative answers in every Krull dimension d≥4: Theorem 4.1, Proposition 5.2 and Corollary 5.3 yield a complex affine integral Poisson algebra with 0 rational but not locally closed; Theorem 3.2 makes 0 primitive. Localization proves its maximal-spectrum core is dense; the Jacobson/Poisson-prime intersection criterion shows that core cannot be locally closed. This is an explicit checked deduction to Brown’s original MaxA question, not a literal claim that Corollary 5.3 names symplectic cores. No all-prime-core assertion or classification of positive subclasses. Published JEMS PDF inspected; separate LWW arXiv v2 all-prime wording is not used. Existing publication; audit: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/1152
